basis: Mitochondrial extraocular myopathy defines PEO; muscle pathology 2/2, ataxia/cerebellar atrophy 1/1. Hearing loss 1/1 omitted at cap; cardiomyopathy 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: PEO is an extraocular skeletal-muscle myopathy; ragged-red fibers in 2/2 and limb weakness support defining muscle disease.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; developmental delay, epileptic encephalopathy and spasticity in 1/1 support neurologic involvement. Optic disc hypoplasia 1-4%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay, epileptic encephalopathy and spasticity in 1/1; these are consequences of the defining mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Adipocytic sarcoma usually arises in deep soft tissue. The 80-99% subcutaneous-nodule annotation conflicts with usual tumor depth; common subcutis occupation is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: none: liposarcoma usually arises in deep soft tissue; the subcutaneous-nodule annotation does not reliably establish common subcutis origin or occupation.

basis: Defining intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies; heart defects ~40-50% and dental anomalies >30%. Qualifying ocular anomalies (HPO 30-79%) omitted at cap; dental defects are more frequent.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: hypodontia and other dental malformations occur in >30% (HPO 30-79%); oral structural defects commonly impair dentition.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: ocular structural abnormalities qualify by HPO 30-79%; defining neurologic/skeletal disease, cardiac defects and more frequent dental defects take priority.

basis: XP/CS defines photosensitive skin disease and neurodegeneration; damaging ocular disease and sensorineural hearing loss are common (>30%) in the overlap phenotype. XPF-specific frequencies are sparse.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is common (>30%) in the Cockayne/XP overlap phenotype; XPF-specific cohorts are very small.

basis: Forebrain malformation; cleft palate 3/4 and dental anomaly 2/4. Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction/DI affects ~50-70% of classic HPE; SIX3-specific frequency uncertain. Individual eye defects 1/4.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: intrinsic hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, especially DI, affects ~50-70% of classic HPE; pituitary agenesis is reported, but SIX3-specific estimates are limited.

basis: Testosterone-to-DHT conversion defect; defining posterior/perineal hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies affect urethral development (HPO 80-99%). Other genital anomalies have no axis.

decisions.renal: primary: posterior/perineal hypospadias is explicitly part of the defining phenotype; urethral malformations fall within renal and are annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder; intellectual disability 5/6, myopathic fibers 2/3 with weakness 2/5, and optic atrophy 2/6 support neurologic, muscle and ocular involvement.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability 5/6, with demyelination 2/2 and cerebellar atrophy, supports common CNS damage from the primary mitochondrial metabolic disorder.

basis: Defining B-cell depletion and cardiomyopathy; absent B cells 3/3, neutropenia 2/3. Bronchiectasis is a separate secondary disease; neurologic findings are not reliably attributable.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis in 1/3 is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections, rather than direct pulmonary involvement by FNIP1 deficiency.

basis: Primary proximal tubulopathy; persistent renal hypophosphatemia and recurrent fractures each annotated 80-99% support mineral and skeletal involvement. Rickets/osteomalacia individually 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: renal phosphate wasting causes persistent hypophosphatemia (HPO 80-99%); this is secondary mineral imbalance from the defining proximal tubulopathy.
